html:
The United States of America is a federal republic in North America, which declared its independence from Britain in 1776 and had it recognised in 1783. It grew from thirteen Atlantic colonies into the largest economy and strongest military power of the 20th century.

The main stages:

  • Founding: thirteen colonies of British North America rebelled, issued the Declaration of Independence and won the Revolutionary War under George Washington. The Constitution of 1787 set up the federal government.
  • Expansion: through purchase, settlement and war, the country spread to the Pacific, taking land from Native nations and, by 1848, about half of Mexico's territory. The California Gold Rush and the transcontinental railroad tied the west to the east.
  • Civil War: the quarrel over slavery led to the American Civil War of 1861 to 1865. Under Abraham Lincoln the Union won and slavery was abolished.
  • Industry and immigration: by 1900 it was the world's largest industrial economy, fed by millions of immigrants (see Ellis Island).
  • World power: it joined both world wars, and after 1945 led the Western side in the Cold War against the Soviet Union.
  • Civil rights: the movement led by Martin Luther King Jr. ended legal segregation in the 1960s.

Its inventions and culture spread worldwide, from the telephone and the airplane to jazz, Hollywood and the internet.
